introduction: These hundred readings are words spoken or written by Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about people who had died: old teachers and young martyrs, mothers, sisters, children, obscure villagers and men of rank, friends remembered years afterwards. They praise service, grieve openly, console the family, honour descendants for the sake of the one who is gone, and ask for visits to a grave. Beside them stand some of the great laments and tributes of other traditions, among them David for Jonathan and for Absalom, Antony for Brutus, Horatio for Hamlet, Pericles for the Athenian dead, Lincoln at Gettysburg, Augustine for his friend and his mother, and Confucius for his disciple, with the proverbs on a good name. A few passages ask what remembrance can do, how much lineage counts, and what to say to a grief that refuses comfort.
questions: These tributes dwell on service, steadfastness and character. If someone spoke about you in the same way, what would you hope they could truthfully say?
Antony says the evil that men do lives after them and the good is buried with them. What have you seen decide how a person is remembered?
Several readings honour children and grandchildren for the sake of a parent, and John the Baptist warns against relying on descent. What does a good ancestor give, and what does it not?
Paul asks people not to sorrow as those without hope, and the readings weep freely. How do grief and faith live together in a bereavement you have known?
George Eliot speaks of those who rest in unvisited tombs. Whose hidden life has shaped yours?
One reading asks for a yearly visit to a friend's grave. What practices of remembrance mean something to you?

outside.why: Paul sums up his own life near its end: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
The master in the parable says: well done, thou good and faithful servant.
Antony says over the body of Brutus: his life was gentle, and the elements so mixed in him that Nature might stand up and say to all the world, This was a man.
Antony begins another funeral speech: the evil that men do lives after them; the good is oft interred with their bones. What decides which part of a life is remembered?
Proverbs says that the memory of the just is blessed, but the name of the wicked shall rot.
David laments Jonathan: how are the mighty fallen; I am distressed for thee, my brother; thy love to me was wonderful.
Genesis says that Abraham died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
George Eliot wrote that the growing good of the world is owing to those who lived faithfully a hidden life, and rest in unvisited tombs.
The psalm says that the righteous shall not be moved for ever, and shall be in everlasting remembrance.
Augustine wrote of the death of a friend: my heart was utterly darkened, and whatever I looked upon was death.
Proverbs says of a good woman: her children arise up, and call her blessed; let her own works praise her in the gates.
Elisha saw his master taken up and cried: my father, my father; and he saw him no more.
Lincoln wrote to a bereaved mother that he felt how weak and fruitless any words of his must be to beguile her from such a loss.
The Preacher says that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, but time and chance happeneth to them all. Is there a wisdom in a sudden death, or only chance?
Ben Jonson wrote that in small proportions we just beauties see, and in short measures life may perfect be. Is a life cut short a lesser life?
The Letter to the Hebrews remembers those who were stoned and slain with the sword, of whom the world was not worthy.
Paul writes to his friends: I thank my God upon every remembrance of you.
Wordsworth called the best portion of a good man's life his little, nameless, unremembered acts of kindness and of love.
Tennyson wrote: but O for the touch of a vanished hand, and the sound of a voice that is still.
The Book of Daniel says that they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.
Horatio says over his friend: now cracks a noble heart; good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
When his best disciple died, Confucius said: alas, Heaven is destroying me.
Jesus said: greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Asked why he loved his dead friend, Montaigne could only answer: because it was he, because it was I.
David went up to the chamber over the gate and wept: O my son Absalom, my son, my son.
At the grave of Lazarus Jesus wept, and those who saw it said: behold how he loved him.
Paul asks the Thessalonians to sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. How do a flood of tears and a firm hope belong together?
Ben Jonson wrote for his dead boy: farewell, thou child of my right hand, and joy.
The Book of Revelation says of the dead: they rest from their labours, and their works do follow them.
Shakespeare has Malcolm say: give sorrow words; the grief that does not speak whispers the o'er-fraught heart and bids it break.
Augustine's mother said: lay this body anywhere; this only I ask, that you will remember me at the Lord's altar.
Acts says that devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.
The council took knowledge of Peter and John, that they had been with Jesus.
Proverbs says that a good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.
Proverbs says that children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers.
Paul remembers the faith that dwelt first in Timothy's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice.
To those who said, Abraham is our father, Jesus answered: if ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham. What does descent from a noble soul give, and what does it demand?
John the Baptist warned: think not to say within yourselves, we have Abraham to our father; God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. How much weight should lineage carry?
Robert Burns sang of honest poverty, and of a worth that owes nothing to rank. Where does true nobility come from?
Proverbs says that the just man walketh in his integrity; his children are blessed after him.
The Qur’an says of those who believe and whose seed follow them in faith: We cause their seed to join them.
Ezekiel says that the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, and the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him. If guilt is not inherited, is merit?
The Qur’an speaks of gardens which they enter along with all who do right of their fathers, their helpmeets and their seed.
The psalm asks that the praises of the Lord be shown to the generation to come.
Whitman wrote of the dead: they are alive and well somewhere; the smallest sprout shows there is really no death.
The psalm says: precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints.
Deuteronomy says that God keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love Him to a thousand generations.
Homer's Hector prays over his small son that one may say of him some day: the son is far better than the father.
Paul tells his friends: ye are our epistle written in our hearts.
The Preacher says that a good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
Luke names certain women who travelled with Jesus and ministered unto him of their substance.
Jesus said that a poor widow who cast in two mites had cast in more than all the rich.
Jesus said of a woman who anointed him: she hath done what she could; this shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
When Dorcas died, the widows stood weeping and shewing the coats and garments which she had made.
Ruth said: whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.
Mary's song begins: my soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
Shakespeare has it said that good name in man and woman is the immediate jewel of their souls.
Paul says that there is neither male nor female, for all are one.
Jesus taught: bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
Tennyson held it true, whatever befell, that it is better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.
David said of his dead child: can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
Lear cries over Cordelia: why should a dog, a horse, a rat have life, and thou no breath at all? What can be said to a grief that will not be consoled?
Jesus said that a corn of wheat, if it die, bringeth forth much fruit.
Jesus said: blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Simeon told the mother of Jesus: a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also.
Isaiah speaks of a Branch that shall grow out of the roots of a felled stem.
The Qur’an says: think not of those who are slain in the way of God as dead; nay, they are living.
Emily Dickinson wrote: because I could not stop for Death, he kindly stopped for me.
Macbeth, hearing of a death, calls life a walking shadow, a poor player that struts and frets his hour upon the stage. What makes a short life more than that?
The church at Smyrna is told: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
Pericles said over the Athenian dead: heroes have the whole earth for their tomb.
Tertullian told the persecutors of his day that the blood of Christians is seed.
The Book of Kings tells of a dead man who revived when he touched the bones of Elisha.
The seer of Revelation is told of those in white robes: these are they which came out of great tribulation.
The Letter to the Hebrews pictures the living as compassed about with a great cloud of witnesses.
Shelley's traveller found the words of a king of kings on a pedestal in the empty desert: look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair. Whose fame endures, and why?
Polycarp, told to deny his Lord, answered that he had served Him eighty and six years.
Lincoln said at Gettysburg that the living cannot hallow the ground; the brave men who struggled there have consecrated it.
Nietzsche said that blood is the very worst witness to truth. What does a martyr's death prove, and what does it not?
Paul lists his own life: in perils of robbers, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness.
The Letter to the Hebrews says of the faithful that they confessed they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
The exiles by the rivers of Babylon wept when they remembered Zion.
Jesus said to the man dying beside him: to day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Deuteronomy says that Moses died in the land of Moab, and no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
The boy Samuel, called by name in the night, ran and answered: here am I.
Genesis says to the first man: dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
The Preacher says that the dead know not any thing, and the memory of them is forgotten. What is a visit to a grave for?
Jesus told a man who wished first to bury his father: follow me, and let the dead bury their dead. How much attention do the dead need from the living?
Paul speaks of being taken from his friends in presence, not in heart.
The Qur’an addresses the soul at peace: return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure.
The psalm says: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
Plato's Socrates tells a young student that wonder is the feeling of a philosopher.
Proverbs says that the king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
Isaiah heard the question, whom shall I send, and answered: here am I; send me.
Proverbs says: my son, forget not my law, but let thine heart keep my commandments.
Longfellow wrote that lives of great men remind us we can make our lives sublime, and leave footprints on the sands of time.
Through Ezekiel God says that He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn and live.
Tennyson hoped to see his Pilot face to face when he had crossed the bar.
Omar Khayyam wrote that the moving finger writes, and having writ, moves on. What in a finished life can still be changed by those who remember it?
Job said: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

samuel-how-are-the-mighty-fallen.text: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places. I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women. How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished

ecclesiastes-good-name-precious-ointment.text: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth. It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart

psalm-everlasting-remembrance.text: Surely he shall not be moved for ever: the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance

john-works-of-abraham.text: They answered and said unto him, Abraham is our father. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham

proverbs-glory-of-children.text: Children's children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers

proverbs-her-children-arise-up.text: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her. Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all. Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates

mark-memorial-of-her.text: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying. Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her

acts-dorcas.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber. And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them. Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them

genesis-gathered-unto-his-people.text: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people

kings-my-father-my-father.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more

acts-devout-men-carried-stephen.text: And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him

philippians-thank-my-god-upon-every-reme.text: I thank my God upon every remembrance of you

analects-heaven-is-destroying-me.text: When Yen Yuan died, the Master said, "Alas! Heaven is destroying me!

pericles-whole-earth-for-their-tomb.text: For heroes have the whole earth for their tomb; and in lands far from their own, where the column with its epitaph declares it, there is enshrined in every breast a record unwritten with no tablet to preserve it, except that of the heart
pericles-whole-earth-for-their-tomb.author: Pericles, as reported by Thucydides
